summary: Iter128 retest of iter127 fixes. VERIFIED FIXED: (1) All spec test IDs are present on both web (dining-home, dining-use-meal-btn, dining-play, dining-pref-veg/nonveg, dining-period-lunch/dinner, dining-spin-btn, dining-surprise-btn, dining-accept-btn, dining-reroll-btn, dining-merchant-page) and mobile (same testIDs); (2) Merchant-role guard on POST /api/merchant/dining-club/redeem — pytest confirms non-owner authed caller gets HTTP 403 {code:'not_meal_merchant'} and admin bypass works. NOT FIXED (blocker still present): (3) MOBILE CORS on the Expo web preview is STILL BROKEN. The backend `CORSMiddleware` is correctly configured (`allow_origin_regex='.*'` + `allow_credentials=True`), but the Kubernetes / Cloudflare ingress in front of the backend REWRITES the `Origin` request header to the internal cluster hostname (`https://mobile-games-v2.cluster-11.preview.emergentcf.cloud`) before it reaches FastAPI. FastAPI echoes back that rewritten origin as `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, but the browser's actual origin is `https://mobile-games-v2.expo.preview.emergentagent.com` → mismatch → browser blocks the response. Confirmed live in the Expo web preview: `/api/auth/demo`, `/api/auth/me` all fail with 'The Access-Control-Allow-Origin header has a value that does not match the origin.' As a result, demo login on mobile FAILS, mobile /dining stays on the login screen, and any authenticated API call is unreachable. Web is unaffected because it is same-origin. WEB happy path partially executed: /dining renders with dining-home + dining-use-meal-btn (test@ user); but test@ had 0 available meal credits (previous backend tests consumed all 3), so clicking Use-a-Meal → /dining/play couldn't reach the wheel spin (blocked by backend `no_available_credits`). Wheel payload schema (segments:int + winner_index:int + winner metadata) confirmed via pytest earlier when a credit was available. Merchant dashboard testids (dining-merchant-page) are wired.

critical.issue: Ingress rewrites the browser Origin header before it reaches FastAPI, so FastAPI's regex-based echo returns the wrong ACAO. Browser blocks ALL /api/* calls from https://mobile-games-v2.expo.preview.emergentagent.com. Backend-level `allow_origin_regex='.*'` alone cannot fix this — either the ingress must preserve the client Origin, OR the mobile Expo web preview must be served under the same host as the API (same-origin), OR the frontend must drop credentials mode for mobile fetches. Verified in-browser (Playwright) with real console errors on /api/auth/demo and /api/auth/me. Reference: /app/backend/server.py:7644-7652.

The third — CORS for the Expo web preview — is NOT actually fixed at the ingress layer even though the backend middleware is correct. The K8s/Cloudflare ingress rewrites the incoming Origin to `https://mobile-games-v2.cluster-11.preview.emergentcf.cloud` before it reaches FastAPI. FastAPI echoes that as ACAO. Browser at `https://mobile-games-v2.expo.preview.emergentagent.com` sees the mismatch and blocks. rca of the issue: Root cause of the remaining CORS block: FastAPI's Starlette CORSMiddleware echoes back the incoming `Origin` header when it matches the configured regex. On this deployment the request passes through a Cloudflare/K8s ingress that normalises the `Origin` header to the internal cluster-facing hostname (`https://mobile-games-v2.cluster-11.preview.emergentcf.cloud`). FastAPI dutifully echoes that normalised value into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. When the browser receives the response, it compares ACAO to its own actual `Origin` (`https://mobile-games-v2.expo.preview.emergentagent.com`), sees a mismatch, and blocks the response. This is why (a) the backend-level regex fix looks correct in code, (b) curl-level headers already reveal the rewritten origin, and (c) the browser confirms the block. Fix must land at either the ingress layer (preserve/pass-through client Origin) OR the app-network layer (frontend to drop credentials on cross-origin mobile fetches OR proxy /api same-origin under the expo host). Same-origin web is unaffected because no cross-origin CORS check is performed at all.
